Often, I see multiple FL Boxes all in close proximity to each other. Sometimes they overlap. For example, here is a EUR-GBP chart. FL Box 3 is important...price breaks the low but cannot sustain the break. We essentially have a FO (on this scale). The origin up is Box 4. ...but then we are faced with a decision to make regarding the importance of FL Box 5 and 6. Which one is more important? Fl Box 5 is formed when price engulfs the top of FL Box 3. FL Box 6 is formed when price engulfs FL Box 2. These two boxes overlap each other... When price returns to this are of overlap, the PA will get confusing regarding EG and FO and MPL. My opinion is that FL Box 5 is most important because it occurred first, and it held price above FL Box 3 which was temporarily breached by an unsustained FO to the downside. Your charts are printed here. lol Hi Staurum I have found that learning how to draw the FL Boxes has helped quite a bit when it comes to identifying engulf vs. fakeout. I used to open a chart and look for fakeouts and engulfs and try to piece together a trade from that perspective. Lately, I have been opening a fresh chart...usually in the middle time frame (hourly is good). I put everything else completely out of my mind..no thoughts about compression or engulfs or PAZ or fakeouts etc.... All I look for are areas where price was held down and I draw the FL Box responsible for holding down price. I do this until I have several levels drawn. When uncertainty arises I will refer to 4-hour or daily time frames. I usually look at the weekly time frame analysis too.. sometimes it helps to see the big picture when drawing the FL Boxes. I avoid drawing any LTF FL Boxes at first. Once have the HTF and middle time frame FL Boxes drawn, I begin to focus on other aspects of trading. Specifically, I start rating the FL Boxes according to their importance. How many times did they bounce price, were they formed as a result of an https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2282-h-s-trading-journal?start=1325 37/65 7/27/2018 H's Trading Journal - Page 54 - RTM Community engulf of a very important zone? Was the FL formed after engulfing a ORFL? HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT With this focus, I identify two or three main FL Boxes that hold special importance and then drop down and look at the PA within the boxes. I draw the major swap zones inside the FL Box. I focus specifically on the three data points that make up a FL Box: the engulf, the RT/FTR, and the breakout (new HH or LL which confirms the FL Box). I find the origin and the fakeouts within the FL Boxes and make note of what levels they are a reaction to. Of course, the MPL is a critical part of this as well. I mark all the MPL's within the targeted FL Boxes. Most recently, I have been focused on learning more about how these zones react with each other. How price moves from zone to zone... I have a hard time keeping track of everything too..I like the triangle picture you posted...it is a good analogy. Your process for identifying and analyzing a chart is just as important as understanding the concepts that RTM teaches. Consistency in the process and steps taken to analyze a chart is critical, and I am still working to find a niche 'focus' when it comes to trading. Everyone processes this information differently, and everyone seems to have their own style of trading. There is no shortage of valuable info on this forum, and it is all important. That said, I think it can be overwhelming at times to focus on too many applications for this knowledge...I am challenging myself to be a more disciplined trader and need to specialize in a particular type of setup that can be replicated over and over again with precise consistency....like a computer. I am still looking for that area of 'specialty'. A good example is Mertch. He knows all the RTM concepts, but he is laser focused on specific QM setups. All his trades are remarkably similar. He has become a master of one type of setup and most likely has executed thousands of trades over the years. I believe this is part of the reason he is such a good trader. I know I didn't offer any solutions to your frustrations, but just know you aren't alone. Or are we supposed to guess the level by taking a few losses on the way? There's always a better level above/below." I don't know the answer to this, but here is something I've been pondering for quite some time now. I look at many successful trades where price reacts exactly as I predict, and my target is hit. Even in these trades, there are MPL's that haven't been hit above my entry. There is always a better level above/below an entry. We can't put a 500+ pip stop on every trade to account for the possibility that price will do some crap like this. What I am coming to believe: The market is reasonably easy to predict if you have the right understanding of why price moves from level to level. I must admit, as unpopular as this viewpoint may be, I don't believe anyone can predict the market 100% of the time...even 90% of time. There are too many external factors that contribute to the global markets to say that there is a secret that will give us 90+ success rate in taking trades. What I think RTM does best is teach a method to analyze the market in a way the cracks the code on how the algorithms work on the super computers that trade most of the IT's capital. The algorithms are predictable because they operate consistently...until they are adjusted/changed. There are so many big players in the market, sometimes an infusion of orders will enter the market and blow through setups that worked in the past. I don't think it is always our fault (sometimes it is) but it may be worth accepting there will be losses...our success depends on how we handle our losses. I don't think we spend enough time taking about this on RTM and it needs to change. All traders lose...and they lose on a regular basis. It his how they handle the losses that determines whether they are successful. I do believe there is chaos (at times) in the market. There is unpredictability (at times) in 19/57 https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2282-h-s-trading-journal?start=1350 7/27/2018 H's Trading Journal - Page 55 - RTM Community the market. That is OK...we shouldn't try to over analyze why every trade goes against HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT us. It is important to autopsy every loss to determine if there was a mistake in the analysis (this is critical) but it's OK to come to the conclusion that the trade failed...there isn't always a reason. Once we can free ourselves from internalizing every loss as 'our fault' we can move past the losses and re focus our efforts on the next setup. EUR-AUD is a good example...I should have been out after the ten pip loss. Instead I got back in and tried to get the next open level of FOF...which got blown through again and again and again. The trade I took yesterday has worked in the past (with regard to my analysis and execution). This time something else occurred, I was wrong, and that is OK. If the market stops out a position, I need to accept it and move on. Tight stops, wide targets. Emotionless trading. If I could sum up RTM and its concepts in a simple way I would say: RTM doesn't contain a special secret or 'holy grail' of trading. It teaches you to understand the market in such a way that you can get in to the market with very limited risk and very wide targets. In my opinion, this is the inherent beauty of the RTM forum and the education here. We trade at the best moments when FOF is likely to exist and reverse price. It doesn't mean we are right all the time...and that is OK. I think it is a waste of time trying to be right 100% of the time. It is impossible. With the right application and through hard work, RTM teaches a method of understanding PA in a way that ensures you will still be wildly successful...even if you are wrong half the time Just my opinion, and I hope I didn't offend anyone! https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2282-h-s-trading-journal?start=1350 20/57 7/27/2018 H's Trading Journal - Page 55 - RTM Community The following user(s) said Thank You: hansma, Jurij, cuimingzhao LOGOUT HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU H's Trading Journal #1360 hoeschec Offline Associate Trader Posts: 1795 Thank you received: 2487 AUD_USD: Missed this entry by two pips last night...so close! Now that an engulf has occurred and FL Box B is confirmed, the origin of the move up is also confirmed as valid...and is the last place with FOF. There is a deep RT to this level before price goes on to hit its target (which is an ORFL). I should have labeled that just 'trick' ...although I don't know if we are supposed to label possible EG as trick. In either case, it seems to me that price still faked out by creating a RBD on a very LTF scale, but once price made a new high the EG is confirmed & a new FL Box is formed. I was labeling as though I was trading live (simulation) and saw the QM reaction. Now that we see the bigger picture, that area was an engulf. Here is another question to ponder: Is every breakout of true supply/demand automatically an EG, or can price FO above true supply demand? Do we have to wait for a new FL box to form or is there a way to know? I think you and Kavya are right. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2282-h-s-trading-journal?start=1425 50/53 7/27/2018 H's Trading Journal - Page 58 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Part of the challenge of back testing, is we can see the EG/FO clearly once PA has unfolded. I have a harder time deciding in real time. In my opinion, FO and EG are often the same thing until we have confirmation of a new high/low, which creates the FL Box in its scale. I'm not sure how to know otherwise... I used to answer to FO/EG question by asking "where did the FO/EG occur"? If the answer was an important area with orders, then I would say it is a FO. If it was an insignificant area, I would label it as an engulf. I'm not sure that is a foolproof way of identifying EG Vs. FO, because we still have the issue of scale to deal with. If we see price EG in to a seemingly unimportant area, and we drop down to a LTF, we may see that it was a significant area for a LTF chart. IF explains this somewhere in a post, but I saved time and made a new screenshot instead of finding it. So the only way to see the DP exactly in real-time is to be looking at a tick chart. However if we cannot check it; as the screenshot shows we assume the whole thing is a DP to break the highs and price can turn anywhere within this kink, so basically we wouldn't trade it if we didn't have a tick chart as our R:R would be bad. In regards to economic news release, I believe its the other way around.
